subject: reference-stencil_y

children.objective: In src/candidate.cu, investigate a single direct-global-load kernel with one output per thread and no shared memory or per-thread multi-output reuse. Map each warp to adjacent X outputs at a fixed Y and Z, then compare suitable block/grid mappings and boundary-index handling. For each neighbor coordinate q=j+d, match the supplied boundary convention: add 63 if q<0, subtract 63 if q>63, otherwise leave q unchanged. Preserve in-range index 63; do not assume endpoint planes are equal. Compute all eight neighbors with the supplied coefficients and produce every output without modifying inputs or relying on scratch contents. Validate signed varying inputs, including independent endpoint values, against the oracle and compare repeated official full-run timings with the baseline.
children.subject: Coalesced direct-global one-output-per-thread kernel

children.objective: In src/candidate.cu, investigate a single shared-memory tiled kernel that loads Y neighborhoods cooperatively with contiguous X lanes and reuses the tile across multiple Y outputs. Explore tile heights and launch shapes while ensuring every required halo is initialized. Match the supplied boundary convention for each neighbor coordinate q=j+d: add 63 if q<0, subtract 63 if q>63, otherwise leave q unchanged; preserve in-range index 63 and do not assume endpoint planes are equal. Preserve the exact stencil, full output, input buffers, and scratch rules. Validate against the oracle on signed varying inputs, including independent endpoint values, then compare repeated official full-run timings with the baseline.
children.subject: Coalesced shared-memory Y tiles with explicit periodic halos

children.objective: In src/candidate.cu, investigate a single kernel where each thread handles several consecutive Y outputs using a register rolling window, with warp lanes still accessing adjacent X values. Explore small output-chunk sizes to balance neighbor reuse against register pressure and occupancy. Do not use shared memory or extra launches in this track. For each neighbor coordinate q=j+d, match the supplied boundary convention: add 63 if q<0, subtract 63 if q>63, otherwise leave q unchanged. Preserve in-range index 63; do not assume endpoint planes are equal. Compute every output for varying signed inputs and preserve the supplied tolerance and buffer constraints. Validate with the oracle and compare repeated official full-run timings with the baseline.
children.subject: Register rolling-window multi-output-per-thread kernel
